The registration fee includes food and drink at aid stations; participant T-shirt if you register by April 30. Registration is final and no on-site registrations are offered. Refunds in case of illness via Startklar insurance (155 SEK) or Startklar Plus (275 SEK). Prize money for 1st-3rd place (10,000 / 7,500 / 5,000 SEK). Accommodation offer: 10% discount at Ski Lodge Tänndalen with code 100MILES; shared accommodation offered for 1,000 SEK per person. Fjällöparveckan offers year-round mountain runs and technique sessions; registration for Tänndalen 100 miles opened September 1, 2025 and the race has a max of 100 runners. The race marks a mountain-adjacent ultramarathon that is part of the larger week of mountain activities in Tänndalen.

images.alt_text: Löpare på en slingrande väg i fjällandskap.

name: Kalmar Malkars 21 km
description: Kalmar Malkars 21 km is a fast, single-loop half marathon that runs through many of Kalmar's beautiful surroundings and is well suited for both competitive runners and recreational participants. Start and finish are at Malkars Training Center on Torsåsgatan, and the course offers views of Kalmar Sound, Kalmar Castle, and the Öland Bridge. In addition to the half marathon, Malkars Femman (5 km) is also offered, which is open to walking, wheelchairs and strollers—movement joy is central. Medals are awarded to all who complete the races.
course_highlights: Single-loop course that passes Kalmar Castle and Kalmar Sound
Views of the Öland Bridge along Ängöleden
Fast course where many set personal records
additional: Start and finish at Malkars Training Center, Toråsgatan 1, Kalmar. Bib pickup: Friday 26 June from 15:00 to 17:00 and Saturday 27 June from 12:00 to 15:00; late registration up to 25 June, afterwards possible at bib pickup. Payment methods for late registration: cash, card or Swish. Hydration stations at the half marathon after 5, 10, 15, 18 km and at the finish (Umara sports drink and water). Everyone who registers for the 21.1 km no later than 20 June will receive a shirt at bib pickup. Medal to all finishers; ICA MAXI provides drinks, fruit and a piece of chocolate after the race. For information: Jonne Svensson 070-693 87 44, Calle Nilsson 070-444 31 02. The half marathon includes hydration stations after 5, 10, 15, 18 km and at the finish; bib numbers collected at designated times; late registration runs until 25 June; payment by card, cash or Swish; a shirt is offered to those who sign up before 20 June; Medal to all finishers.

name: Jordgubbslunken
description: Jordgubbslunken is a popular rural race in Rudskoga with the motto "gå, lunka, löp" (walk, plod, run). The race offers Lilla Lunken (6 km) and Stora Lunken (10 km) as well as a Minilunken for children (born -17 or later). Start and finish are at Grunnebacka skola, and the courses follow Rudskoga's winding village roads through a beautiful cultural countryside. At the finish, all participants receive a liter of strawberries, and there is a generous prize table as well as a grand prize drawn from the bib number.
course_highlights: 6 km loop on gravel surfaces
10 km loop that alternates between gravel roads and neatly cut grass
Start and finish at Grunnebacka skola; courses follow winding village roads through a cultural countryside
additional: Always the first Saturday after Midsummer; Categories for men, women and children; Minilunken for children born -17 or later; All participants receive a liter of strawberries at the finish; Generous prize table and a grand prize drawn on the bib number; Information for this year's race will be published under "På gång i Rudskoga" on the website. The surface on the 6 km loop is gravel, while the 10 km loop alternates between gravel road and well-kept grass. Start at 15:00. Registration on site no later than 14:30 (on-site registration for a higher fee). Payment via Bankgiro 505-1404 or Swish 1233296605; questions to the listed phone numbers are in the information.

name: H2 Trail
distance_verbose: 50 miles, 50 km, 28 km, 18 km, 10 km, 5 km
description: Umara H2 Trail 2026 is the OK Skogsvargarnas trail race that takes place on Saturday, June 27, starting from the Bergagården competition center on Hunneberg. The race program includes several distances (80 km, 50 km, 28 km, 18 km, 11 km, 6 km) as well as a kids' and mini-trail for the youngest participants. The courses run across Halle and Hunneberg and offer viewpoints, cottages, and swimming spots in varied terrain. The event features family-oriented elements for children and practical information about equipment and safety on the website.
course_highlights: The course traverses the Halle and Hunneberg plateau mountains with several viewpoints.
Terrain: majority of trails (about 73%), plus gravel roads (23%), and a little asphalt (4%).
Technical and challenging downhill at Krösa Klev, marked with extra signs.
additional: Race center: Bergagården, parking about 300 meters from the center (follow the signs). Course marking with blue arrows and blue-white tape markers. All participants must carry their own fluids and own mug (mugs available for sale at the race center). Availability of support at two designated locations along the course (Halleberg turnaround and Hunneberg north of Fristorps Gransjö, as well as at the Bergagården turnaround). Recommended headlamp for late starters (especially for the 80 km); mobile phone and power bank recommended. Knatte-/minitrail and miniknat have a separate, family-friendly setup, a medal for all participants and a price of 50 SEK (late/on-site registration for the children's races). Showers and a sauna are available in the clubhouse at Bergagården. Race center: Bergagården, Hunneberg. Start times by distance: 80 km 08:00, 50 km 08:00, 28 km 10:00, 18 km 09:00, 11 km 10:15; Knatte trail starts approx 10:45/11:00. Knatte-/minitrail and miniknat for the youngest age groups.

name: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi
location: Ottsjö, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Fjällmaraton Gastronomi is a non-competitive mountain event where participants can choose between two point-to-point routes (approximately 24 km or 42 km) and enjoy both the mountain scenery and local food. The courses are marked and the food stations (roughly every 7 km) serve local ingredients prepared and served on the mountain in collaboration with local producers. For 2026, new routes have been developed: the longer course starts and finishes in Ottsjö, while the shorter starts in Trillevallen and finishes in Ottsjö. The event has open start times so participants can experience it at their own pace, but it is recommended to start early if planning to hike slowly.
course_highlights: Point-to-point in mountain terrain with both 24 km and 42 km options
Food stations about every 7 km offering local mountain dishes prepared and served on site
2026 routes: the longer course starts and finishes in Ottsjö; the shorter course starts in Trillevallen and finishes in Ottsjö
additional: Non-competitive format with open starts; recommended to start early for slow hikers. Transfers to the start are available and can be booked (transfer bookings open about two weeks before the race). The organizer recommends accommodations at Trillevallens Högfjällshotell or in Ottsjö (contact details are on the page). Event memos contain details about transport and logistics. Open start times to allow a relaxed pace; aid stations roughly every 7 km featuring local producers; accommodation suggestions at Trillevallens Högfjällshotell or Ottsjö; bus transfers to the start from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker; electronic timing and transport logistics managed by the event.

name: Silverleden Ultra
description: Silverleden Ultra is a trail race in Hällefors/Bergslagen with distances of 64 km, 33 km and 100 miles. The race takes place 26–27 June 2026 and is marketed under the slogan 'runner's joy' — technical, hilly nature with lots of trails and climbing awaiting the participants. The 100-mile race is fully booked for 2026. The organizer's wording and information emphasize nature-focused, demanding courses where proper equipment is recommended.
course_highlights: Hilly terrain with many climbs – the larger climbs are mainly in the second half of the course.
Technical trail with roots and rock slabs; trail shoes with a rugged tread are recommended.
The course passes the checkpoint at Silvergruvan (referred to as a checkpoint after about 35 km).
additional: Praktiskt: Bus to the start for the 33 km leaves Hurtigtorpet at 10:30 and must be booked in advance (booking option available until 2026-06-20); payment outside card can be made to IBAN SE09 9020 0000 0906 0545 6739 with the reference number from registration; there are limited camping spots for caravans/motorhomes — please notify via info@silverledenultra.se (limited electricity); no relay team registrations possible in 2026; minimum age 15 years (in the year you turn) for participants; the 33 km can be completed under parental supervision even if younger; receipts from the registration system serve as documentation for wellness subsidy; equipment recommendations: trail shoes are recommended and metal studs are not recommended; poles are used rarely but can be recommended for the second half of the course and can be taken to the Silvergruvan checkpoint; GPX and Strava links are available; maximum time is 12 hours; energy checkpoints along the course; maps and course descriptions are available on the website.

name: Bocksten Trailrun
location: Öströö Fårfarm, Åkulla Bokskogar, Varberg Municipality, Halland County, Sweden
distance_verbose: Marathon, 24 km, Halvmarathon, 12 km, 6.7 km, 5 km
description: Bocksten TrailRun is a nature-centered trail race with the competition center at Öströö sheep farm and courses in the Åkulla beech forests. The event offers four distances (5 km, 12 km, 22 km and Ultra 44 km) through beech forest, spruce forest, lake views and varied trails. The races are spectator-friendly, have limited entry slots and a special medal for participants. Come and experience the joy of running and the sense of community in a magical forest setting.
course_highlights: Running in the Åkulla beech forests and enchanted spruce forests
Varied terrain: technical trails, off-trail sections and gravel roads with lake views
Many elevation gains and scenic views; also a 6.7 km loop for Vineyard Backyard Ultra
additional: Distance options: 5 km (start 10:15, 200 places), 12 km (start 10:00, 400 places), 22 km (start 10:30, 300 places) and Ultra 44 km (start 08:00, 100 places). Total number of starting spots is limited (only 1000 places). GPS coordinates for the competition center: 57.06881078975495, 12.506526026672418. During the event only tap water is used (no plastic bottles); Tailwind and juice are available as alternatives. For the Vineyard Backyard Ultra, your own cup/mug is mandatory; headlamp and personal medication are mandatory, and the headlamp must be worn from 20:00 to 07:00. Bib pickup and registration are handled in the start area (times given in the invitation); if you need assistance contact the race management at 076-8159678. There is an option to purchase Startklar cancellation and accident insurance (prices listed in the invitation). The summer edition takes place on June 27, 2026 with the distances 5/12/22/Ultra 44 km; the winter edition is held at Öströö Farm with 5/12/24 km and 500 places, accommodations can be booked via Åkulla Resort with a discount (code bockstentrailrun). The Backyard Ultra race at Ästad Vineyard has a 6.7 km course and starts every full hour.

name: Kustmaran (Kristianopel)
distance_verbose: Marathon, Halvmarathon, 10 km, 5 km, 2.5 km, 0.9 km
description: Kustmaran and Kristianopel Runt is a running festival for the whole family in picturesque Kristianopel on the east coast, with distances from 0.9 km up to the marathon (42.2 km). The event takes place on June 27, 2026 and offers both competitive races and recreational options, as well as engaged support from Team Blekinge's volunteers. The day combines running in an idyllic summer landscape with opportunities for swimming, dining, and overnight stays in the area. Everyone is welcome, from children's races and walking/Sommarlunken without timing to half- and full-marathon for more experienced runners.
course_highlights: Running in an idyllic summer landscape around picturesque Kristianopel on the east coast
Range of courses: marathon (42.2 km), half marathon (21.1 km), 10 km, 5 km, 2.5 km, 0.9 km (children's race) and Sommarlunken 4 km
The children's race takes place at Kristianopels Camping; opportunities for swimming and services in the village
additional: Bib pickup and late registration can be done on race day from 08:00. Payment at standard registration is by card or Swish; for bank giro payments please contact register@teamblekinge.nu before registration. Electronic timing is provided by Racetimer. Half marathon and marathon require that the participant is at least 17 years old during the year. Sommarlunken is without timing and no medal is awarded; there are prize draws. Start times vary by distance; electronic timing; registration and payment options: card and Swish for standard registration, bank giro via contact if needed; late registration via Swish or cash; parking outside Kristianopel; hydration and changing facilities, toilets and medical care at the finish area; rules according to Svenska Friidrottsförbundet.

name: TrailÖvik
description: TrailÖvik is a welcoming trail race in Själevad on June 28, 2026, with several courses (Mini, 6 km, 12 km, 22 km and Night Edition) that suit both recreational runners and elite runners. The courses run through stunning nature with technical singletracks, hilly terrain and several viewpoints over the Höga Kusten World Heritage Site. The event is described as both family-friendly and professional, with trial runs, maps and service along the course. The arena and start/finish are at the Skogslöparnas clubhouse, and the race has been praised for its varied and challenging routes.
course_highlights: Stunning nature and views over Höga Kusten, including from the summit of Mycklingberget
Technical trail sections with steep parts, a stair climb up Mycklingberget, and ropes at certain passages
The 22 km course includes three hilltops, mires, stream ravines and hydration stations (sports drink and water)
additional: The arena/start and bib distribution are on the gravel area below the Skogslöparnas clubhouse (Nordhemsvägen 41, 89430 Själevad); bibs must be collected no later than 30 minutes before start; the PM will be published 10 days before the competition; registration is via Mittlopp and late registration opens at the arena and closes 30 minutes before the respective start; trial runs and maps are available (physical maps in the mailbox at the start of Älgstråket and downloadable maps); livestream and live results are provided; recommendation to wear studded shoes in wet weather and information about hydration checks (22 km: first check at approximately 4 km with sports drink and water). Four distances and Night Edition; start around 11:00; registration via Mittlopp; the arena is located below the Skogslöparnas clubhouse in Själevad (Nordhemsvägen 41); maps/trial runs and marking of the course are offered; results are shown live at the arena and online.

name: Böda Sandsloppet
location: Böda Sand SportCamp, Böda Sand, Öland, Sweden
description: Böda Sandsloppet is a family-friendly recreational run held at Böda Sand on Öland by Högby IF athletics. The race offers several distances for adults and youths - 6.5 km and 4 km for adults, and 1.8 km and 1 km for youths - with start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp. All finishers receive a medal, and the highlight of the meal category is sausages served after the finish. Registration is via olandrunning.se or on-site, and the last registration day is 26 June 2026 (with late registration until 1 July).
course_highlights: Forest terrain along the Böda Sand area on Öland
Distances for adults: 6.5 km and 4 km; for youths: 1.8 km and 1 km
All finishers receive a medal and sausages are served after the finish
additional: Start and finish at Böda Sand SportCamp. Last registration day 26 June 2026; late registration until 1 July. Registration via olandrunning.se or on-site. Payment by cash, card or Swish.

name: Byrundan
location: Unos Park, Gamleby, Västervik Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Byrundan is a city race that takes place in Gamleby with start and finish in Unos Park. The competition offers races for all ages and is well suited for both recreational runners and families. Join us on July 3, 2026 — registration opens soon.
course_highlights: Runs through Gamleby (urban setting)
Start and finish in Unos Park
Race for all ages
additional: Registration opens soon; start and finish in Unos Park; race is offered for all ages; organizer's postal address: C/o Lena Persson, Lapserums Gård, 594 92 Gamleby. The race is held indoors in Unos Park; registration opens soon ahead of 2026-07-03.

name: Strömstadmilen
description: Strömstad Mile is organized by Strömstad Löparklubb and takes place on Saturday, July 4, 2026. The race offers runner-friendly distances through central Strömstad when Bohuslän is at its most beautiful, with the course lined by dense spectator crowds. The main course is an exactly measured 5 km loop that can be run one or two laps (5 km or 10 km); start and finish are at Strömsvallen. Everyone is welcome - there are also children's classes and a walking class for those who want to experience the race without timing.
course_highlights: Runner-friendly 5 km loop through Strömstad center (can be run as 1 or 2 laps for 5/10 km)
The course is lined with spectators and clearly marked with plenty of signage
Start and finish at Strömsvallen; lap turning takes place in the outer lanes according to instructions
additional: Bib number pickup and late registration: Friday, July 3 from 15:00 - 18:00 at Strömstad Shoppingcenter and on race day from 09:30 at Strömsvallen. The T-shirt can be pre-ordered with the registration no later than June 7 (199 kr) and picked up with the bib; sizes for children and adults are offered. Timing ends at 16:45. Limited number of parking spaces at Strömsvallen; alternative parking at Strömstad Gymnasium (~500 m). All finishers receive a specially designed medal; photographers are along the course and a selection of photos will be published on Facebook/Instagram after the race. New walking class approximately 3 km along Strömstadvattnet; start and finish at Friluftsmuseet/Fiskartorpet; start time 11:00; the distances include 10 km as two laps of 5 km, 5 km, 4 km walking, 1 mil for ungdomar and 1 km for yngsta barn; bib numbers and late registration via Strömstad Shoppingcenter or Strömsvallen; T-shirt, medal, prize presentation, parking and other logistics.

tiers.description: Early Bird! T o m 2 Mars

description: Kolmården Ultra Trail is a welcoming yet demanding trail race for both elite runners and recreational runners. Choose between longer challenges (45 km or 60 km) where the course takes you through Kolmård Forest, up the Kvarseboklints ridge, down to the Bråviken shore, past Nävsjön Nature Reserve, and finally through the technical Bråviksbranten before the finish line. The race combines technical trails, boardwalks over bogs, and stunning views, and offers well-equipped aid stations along the way. The organizers emphasize safety and mandatory equipment, as well as a finishing medal and simpler refreshments at the finish.
course_highlights: The mighty Kvarseboklints ridge with views
Descent to Bråviken's shore and crossing Nävsjön with boardwalks over expansive bogs
Technical and demanding running through the Bråviksbranten nature reserve
additional: Mandatory equipment: mobile phone, running vest/backpack with fluids (at least 0.5 L), pressure bandage/bleeding stopper and a map with an emergency number (distributed at bib pickup). Hydration stations: 45K = 4 stations, 60K = 5 stations (for the 48 km variant, detailed stations with various energy products are provided). Bib pickup from 05:30; bib must be collected no later than 30 minutes before start. Course marking with large orange arrows and tape markers. At the finish, lighter refreshments and a self-designed medal are included; massage is offered at cost. Energy/fluids in collaboration with Umara. Mandatory equipment; start times: 45K 08:00; cut-off time at 44 km: 13:30; hydration stations: 45K 4 stations, 60K 5 stations; finish: meal included in the registration fee.

name: Läckövarvet
organizer: Kroppslabbet; Språng träning & äventyr; Stiftelsen Läckö Slott
description: Welcome to Läckövarvet – a running race with start and finish at the magnificent Läckö Slott on Kållandsö. The race is offered in 21 km, 10 km and a 2 km children's race and offers varied terrain with forest trails, gravel roads and shorter asphalt sections, as well as views of Vänern. The course passes well-known places such as Spikens Fiskehamn and Roparudden and ends with a lap through the moat around the castle. The race targets both competitive runners and families who want to enjoy a nature-based and culturally historic running experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain: forest trails, gravel roads and shorter asphalt sections
The course passes Spikens Fiskehamn and technical, scenic trails on Roparudden (cliffs and winding paths)
Starting and finishing at Läckö Slott with a concluding lap through the moat and finish in front of the castle gate
additional: Courses start outside Läckö Slott; fluids/energy along the course; medical services and showers on site; lunch package for 165 kr after finishing; parking 50 kr; bus to the race is recommended; included in the Västsvenska Löparcupen.

name: Mörksuggejakten TrailRun
description: Mörksuggejakten is a classic long-distance cup race in Rättvik, appreciated by both elite cyclists and recreational riders. The main course is available as 72 km or a shortened 44 km variant and offers varied terrain with gravel roads, trails, and some significant climbs as well as nice views over Siljan. The course passes places such as Vidablick, Hedsåsens fäbodar, the Enåns valley with narrow suspension bridges, as well as Dalhalla and Springkällan. The event also includes Lilla Mörksuggejakten for youths in the Jarl area and is organized by IK Jarl.
course_highlights: Main course 72 km (alternative 44 km short variant)
Views over Siljan from Vidablick and Hedsåsens fäbodar
Sections along the Enåns valley with narrow suspension bridges; features at Dalhalla and Springkällan
additional: Registration for competitive classes takes place via RaceWeb; late registration is handled on RaceWeb between 08:30 - 12:00 (Lilla Mörksuggan). Bib-number distribution for Lilla Mörksuggejakten: Jarlstugan Saturday 5 July from 09:00 to 11:30; bib numbers with chips are used in competitive classes and in recreation/family classes (knatte, recreation/family no timing). Technical zone and fueling are available in the arena between the start and finish zones; medical staff are on site (responsible Josefin Linell, tel. 076-796 39 69). Changing rooms and showers are available at Jarlstugan. The premiere of Mörksuggejakten TrailRun was in 2017. The race is part of the Mörksuggejakten activities in Rättvik and coordinated with Lilla Mörksuggejakten; late registration and bib numbers are handled according to the plans for 4 July 2026.

name: Semesterhalvmaran
location: Fjugesta, Laxå Municipality, Örebro County, Sweden
description: Semester Half Marathon is a summer race organized by the running club LK Gränslöst that gives runners the opportunity to experience the beautiful expanse of Närkeslätten. The course often runs on gravel roads among rolling grain fields and offers a nature-focused, summery running experience. LK Gränslöst is an inclusive club that welcomes runners of all levels.
course_highlights: Gravel roads on Närkeslätten
Rolling grain fields and open views
Summer/holiday-season race with a calm, nature-focused character
additional: LK Gränslöst organizes several summer races: Semester Half Marathon, Summer Mile and the children's race Solruset. The club announced that the races will be paused during 2025 due to limited availability of key personnel in the organizing group. The club also offers open Wednesday training sessions at 18:00 in Örebro (location varies) led by Carina Gustavsson and Thomas Stenius.

name: Gotland Run 511k (2026)
description: Gotland Run 511k is more of a running adventure than a traditional race: a self-supported journey around Gotland of about 511 km with start and finish in Visby. Participants follow a clockwise loop that also includes a lap around Fårö, and receive support from four so-called Angel Stations along the way. The organizer provides some basic services, but runners are responsible for most of the food and logistics arrangements. The whole route must be completed on foot within 10 days, with regular position reports around the clock.
course_highlights: Circular route around Gotland (start and finish in Visby) including a lap around Fårö
Most of the route follows Gotlandsleden: long asphalt stretches, gravel roads and shorter trail sections
Four Angel Stations along the course offering water, support and sometimes the option for a short rest or bed
additional: Self-sufficiency format: the organizer provides only the most basic services; participants are responsible for food and most of the lodging/logistics. Mandatory pre-race dinner and mandatory race briefing in Visby the evening before the start. Includes one night of lodging at Visby Prison Hostel (one night) as well as breakfast on the start morning, race number, baggage storage during the race and a souvenir for those who complete. Transport back to Visby is offered for participants who withdraw from the race. Participants must report position twice daily (10:00 and 22:00) via an online check-in tool and a Google Maps link. Total time limit 10 days (average ~51 km per day). There are sections on mandatory equipment and basic rules on the information page. History: the first edition in 2023 had 5 starters and 3 finished. Distance approximately 511 km (318 miles); four Angel Stations along the route; no pacing; mandatory equipment; pre-race dinner and briefing; one night of lodging in Visby included; baggage storage; race number; transport back to Visby upon withdrawal; finishers receive a souvenir.

name: Killebom Loppet Sölvesborg
description: Sölvesborg's Killebom Run offers multiple formats and distances to choose from that suit both the slower and the faster runner. Since it is an ongoing city festival, there will certainly be a lot of movement and spectators cheering on all participants. Of course, our wonderful volunteers will make sure to encourage and cheer you on out on the course. Distances to choose from are the children's race (approximately 400 meters), 5 km, or 10 km (the 10 km loop course). All proceeds from the children's race go to Barncancerfonden, so take the opportunity to do a good deed and run with the whole family.

images.alt_text: Två kvinnor under en välkomstportal vid ett löplopp.
Tre män i löparkläder med nummerbrickor står vid en hamn, redo för Killebom Loppet.
Deltagare i en löpartävling på en landsväg, med tydliga nummerlappar och löparutrustning.
Människor i varselvästar organiserar papper vid ett bord under ett event.

name: Västervik City Run
description: Västervik City Run is an urban race of 6.2 km in and around the centre of Västervik with start and finish at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget. The course consists of two roughly 3 km long loops with a turnaround over Fiskaretorget. The race has been organized since 2011 and traditionally takes place on the Monday in week 28 with start at 20:00. The race is well established in Västervik and attracts runners of various ages.
course_highlights: City Run, 6.2 km (two loops of ~3 km)
Start and finish at Grönsaks- och Fiskartorget
Turnaround at Fiskaretorget
additional: Children's race (Sparbanksloppet) is an 800 m kids' race for children up to 10 years with a common start from Fiskaretorget at 18:30; the start for the kids' race takes place at approximately Stegeholms slottsruin by the sun deck and Myntbryggan and follows the cycle path along Gamlebyviken to the finish at Grönsakstorget. After finishing the kids' race, participants are awarded a medal. Bib pickup at ICA Maxi or the race secretariat; pre-registration closes July 3 at 16:00; registration on race day 13:00 - 19:00.

name: Nordansjö Nattultra
location: Norbergs OK:s klubbstuga, Nordansjö 24, Norberg, Sweden
description: Nordansjö Nattultra is a nature-oriented ultrarunning experience that takes place during the night of July 10–11, 2026, with the main race at 60 km divided into five loops. The race is organized by Norbergs OK with start and finish at the club cabin in Nordansjö, and it suits both experienced ultrarunners and runners who want to try a longer summer challenge. The course is easy to run and designed to provide a pleasant summer experience with both camaraderie and competition. Warm welcome to the second edition of Nordansjö Nattultra!
course_highlights: Five loops of 12 km (60 km total)
Mainly rights-of-way and gravel roads, with about 2.7 km on a lit trail
The course is run clockwise and includes five downhill sections down Håberget
additional: Mandatory equipment: headlamp and mobile phone. Maximum time for 60 km is 10 hours; finish after five loops (5×12 km). Bib numbers can be collected from 19:00 Friday 10 July at the club cabin. Water checkpoints at start/finish and at the halfway point (6 km); no disposable cups are provided - bring your own soft bottle or cup. Upon completing the race you receive a finisher cap, a medal, and breakfast at the club cabin. Maximum 100 participants (first come, first served). Berg prize on Håberget; start/finish at Norbergs OK's Nordansjö club cabin (Nordansjö 24, Norberg); max 100 participants; water checkpoints at start, finish and halfway; no mugs provided - bring your own cup/kåsa; registration opened 2025-09-01.

name: Musköloppet
location: Muskö Hembygdsgård, Muskö, Haninge kommun, Stockholms län, Sverige
description: Muskö Run is a traditional jogging race in a grand archipelago setting with a start and finish at Muskö Hembygård / Muskö IF's clubhouse. The race typically attracts around 300 runners (about 400 including kids) and has a friendly, homecoming atmosphere where many take the opportunity to meet relatives and neighbors. The competition offers children's and youth classes as well as recreational classes (5 km and 10 km) on varied surfaces and is scheduled to take place on Saturday, July 11, 2026.
course_highlights: Start/finish at Muskö Hembygård near the clubhouse, outdoor gym and hockey rink
Course surface: approximately 50% asphalt, 30–40% gravel and 10% terrain
5- and 10-km courses are officially measured (course measurer Mikael Hill, 240523) and the 10-km is run as one lap this year
additional: Late registration takes place at the start/finish area no later than one hour before the race start. Food and drinks are available at the start/finish. Get There information with driving and public transport directions and parking instructions is available on the 'Hitta hit' page. Around 300 runners typically participate (about 400 including kids). Start and finish area at Muskö Hembygård / Muskö IF's clubhouse; 5- and 10-km courses with varied surfaces (approximately 50% asphalt, 40% gravel, 10% terrain on one course; approximately 60% asphalt, 30% gravel, 10% terrain on the other); marketing, kiosk goods, coffee, soft drinks, and refreshments from Mickes Grill; late registration at the finish area no later than one hour before the race starts.

name: Lidingöloppet Funäsfjällen
description: Lidingöloppet in Funäsfjällen is "Sweden's most beautiful challenge" - a cross-country terrain race with steep climbs, sloping trails, open meadows and expansive mountain vistas. The third edition will be held on 11 July 2026 and offers an unbeatable combination of adrenaline and nature experiences. A warm welcome to Bruksvallarnas ski stadium where you register via Lidingöloppet's website and collect your race bib on-site.
course_highlights: Steep climbs and challenging mountain terrain
Sloping trails and flat meadow areas
Expansive mountain vistas and panoramic views
additional: Registration via the Lidingöloppet website; bib distribution takes place on-site in Bruksvallarna. When registering on race day (Saturday), a fee of 100 kr is added. The week before, Bruksvallarnas running week is held with shoe tests, running clinics, children's activities, after run and expo at Arena Syd outside Bruksvallarnas SportCenter. The results will be official and finalized one week after the race. By registering you agree that your name will be published in start and results lists and that images may be used in the event's channels; deviations are handled by the organizers' office (info@lidingoloppet.se). Seeding and start times; accommodation in Ramundberget near the start location; opportunities for logistics such as parking, hydration stations and food and drinks; a week in July with a program and accommodation information via bruksvallsliden.se/lidingoloppet; children's run/adventure for younger participants

name: Klåveröd Backyard 2026
description: Klåveröd Backyard 2026 is a Facebook-published event in Svalöv that takes place on Saturday, July 11, 2026, created by Linda Bengtsson. The event is linked to Klåveröds Skidklubb and is presented via an official Facebook event page. The location is Klåveröd near Söderåsen, which provides opportunities for trail- and cross-country running in a nature-rich environment. For details and contact information, please refer to the event page on Facebook.
course_highlights: Running in Klåveröd/Svalöv near Söderåsen
Trail- and cross-country terrain (organized via Klåveröds Skidklubb)
Proximity to Söderåsen's nature and national park area
additional: Organizer/creator: Linda Bengtsson; event linked to Klåveröds Skidklubb; main information page and invitation are available as a Facebook event: https://www.facebook.com/events/1496584765165217/; Klåveröd's Facebook group and page are used for local information. Previous Klåveröd Backyard 2024: winner Jonas Elmer with 14 laps, about 90 km total.

name: Kraftprovet
organizer: Trollhättans IF Friidrott och Trollhättans SOK
description: Kraftprovet is a classic city race in the heart of Trollhättan and on July 17, 2026 will celebrate its 40th anniversary. The course follows the canal area through green corridors with varied and hilly terrain, and offers beautiful views of the Göta älv, the locks and the historic power stations. The race attracts both elite runners and recreational runners and contributes to a folk festival with spectators, music and activities for the whole family. The organizers are Trollhättans IF Friidrott and Trollhättans SOK.
course_highlights: The course runs along the canal area and the locks and falls area in Trollhättan
Varied and hilly terrain with clearly marked kilometer markers
Views of the Göta älv, the locks and the historic power stations
additional: Start and finish at Hansenplatsen in Trollhättan. Bib number and T-shirt are picked up at the start/finish area from 10:00 and distribution closes 30 minutes before each start. Names printed on the bib at registration no later than June 30. Opportunity to order a functional T-shirt at registration no later than May 15 (included for Kraftprovet 11.6 km and Specialprovet; costs 130 SEK for the other races). Specialprovet welcomes assistants/companions at no extra cost. Kraftprovet has pacers for 50, 55 and 60 minutes; Fun Run is untimed. A silver medal is awarded for times under 50:00 (men) and 55:00 (women). Costume contest gathers at 15:45 with a prize pool for best costume. 40th anniversary with new race elements; Knatteprovet, Miniprovet and the 800 m race are part of the lineup; there is an option to buy this year's T-shirt in connection with registration.

name: Helags Fjällmara
distance_verbose: Marathon, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3000 meter, 0.8 km
description: Helags Fjällmara is a classic mountain trail race in the Ljungdalsfjällen range, organized since 1985. The event offers several distances for different levels, from the children's run up to longer mountain trail races, and features beautiful views and challenging trails. Start and finish are located on the meadow in the middle of the village of Ljungdalen, providing a pleasant race venue for both elite runners and families. The event is organized on a voluntary basis by Ljungdalens Gymnastik och Idrottsförening.
course_highlights: Mountain trail racing with beautiful views and challenging trails
Start and finish on the meadow in Ljungdalen
Several distances for different levels (23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m)
additional: Practical information: registration is open until 16/7 (no on-site late registration); registration for the children's run is open until 18/7 at 10:15. Participant caps: 23 km 250 participants, 12 km 200, 5 km 150, 3 km 100, 800 m 200. The registration fee includes energy and hydration stations along the course, a personal mug from Umara (bring it to the race), electronic timing (chip in the bib) and a medal for all finishers. Showers and a sauna are available after finishing. Registration is binding; transfer of entry and class changes are possible for a change fee of SEK 250 (changes according to instructions via email; the registration page mentions contacts at both info@ljungdalensgif.se and hej@helagsfjallmara.se). Competition classes for elite, recreational runners and children; registration takes place via RaceWeb on the website; several distances available: 42 km, 23 km, 12 km, 5 km, 3 km and 800 m.

name: Hornsjön Runt
location: Pensionat Hornsjön, Löttorp, Borgholm Municipality, Kalmar County, Sweden
description: Hornsjön Run is a family-friendly running event that goes around Öland's only inland lake, with beautiful and varied surroundings. The race is organized by Högby IF and offers distances for children and youth, 5.5 km, 11 km, and a walking class without timing. Start and finish at Pensionat Hornsjön, and all finishers receive a medal. The event combines a long tradition with scenic courses over gravel, sand dunes, forest and open pastures.
course_highlights: Around Öland's only inland lake (Hornsjön)
Varied surfaces: gravel with Öland limestone, grass and sand dunes
Passes cattle pastures as well as deciduous and coniferous forest; three water stations along the course
additional: Registration by July 11, 2026; late registration through July 16, after which there is the option to register at the bib-number pickup from 12:00 on race day. Walking class (without timing) with start times between 13:00 and 16:00. Three water stations along the course as well as water at the start/finish. Possibility of showers and changing at Högby Sports Ground. Prize presentation to the top three in all classes and raffle prizes. Start times: youth classes 15:30; 5.5 km 17:00; 11 km 17:05. Walking class available (5.5 or 11 km) with start times between 13:00 and 16:00. Showers and changing at Högby Sports Ground.

name: Runmaröloppen 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Mini-Lunken 1.5km 60kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och en kula glass.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lunken 5.7km: från 150kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Halvmarathon 21km: från 350kr inkl nummerlapp, medalj och finisherdryck.

description: RUNmaröloppen is a family-friendly race in the heart of Stockholm's archipelago on Runmarö, with start and finish at the pub Svängen. The event offers short children's races, Lunken (5.7 km) and a half marathon (21 km) over beautiful trails, open fields and archipelago villages — perfect as a day trip with Waxholmsbåtarna. The races are limited in participant numbers and place a strong emphasis on atmosphere, energy stations and sustainability; 20% of the surplus goes to Skärgårdsstiftelsen.
course_highlights: Half marathon (21 km) around the entire Runmarö with views toward Sandhamn
A mix of trail paths, gravel roads and archipelago villages; two trail sections on the half marathon
Fixed signs and 1 km markers on the half marathon, as well as many local energy stations
additional: Start and finish at the pub Svängen (about 400 m from the pier). Mini-Lunken starts at 11:00; Lunken and the Halvmarathon start at 13:00. The Halvmarathon has 1 km markers, an interactive map, total elevation gain of 169 m and several local water stations (for example Nore with salted cucumber and Solberga). Mini-Lunken participants receive an ice cream; everyone receives a medal and a finisher drink. The races have limited numbers (200 places for the Halvmarathon and 120 for Lunken in the first round, with a further 30 places released closer to the event, often at 18:00 the day before). Registration opens May 1 at 09:00. 20% of the surplus is donated to Skärgårdsstiftelsen. Results are published online and prize giving takes place after the races; in the evening there is a dinner/party at Svängen. Start and finish at Svängen; courses marked; registration starts May 1 at 09:00; a significant number of places are limited (Halvmarathon 200 places, Lunken 120 in the first round, plus 30 extra places later); a purposeful charitable angle and local atmosphere.

name: Löttorpsvarvet
location: First Camp Löttorp, Löttorp, Öland, Sweden
description: Löttorpsvarvet is a family-friendly cross-country race held at First Camp Löttorp on Öland. The main distance is 6.2 km and the course runs through forest and meadowland with nice views of the Baltic Sea. There are youth classes of 1.4 km and 800 m for younger runners, and a medal is awarded to all who complete the race. The organizer is Högby IF and the event welcomes both recreational runners and youths.
course_highlights: 6.2 km in lovely terrain around First Camp Löttorp
Running through forest and meadowland with views of the Baltic Sea
Youth courses 1.4 km and 800 m
additional: Registration by July 15, 2026. Late registration allowed until July 20; thereafter the option to register at bib pickup on race day (from 3:00 PM). Late registration fee: 300 SEK for Men/Women and 200 SEK for Children/Youth. Payments accepted in cash, by card or Swish. Children/Youth classes: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9, P/F11, P/F13 (1.4 km) with separate start times; classes 11 years and younger have no timing/prize awarding. Medal to all who complete the race. Inquiries: Jonne Svensson 070-693 87 44, Calle Nilsson 070-444 31 02. Registration by July 15, 2026; late registration until July 20; thereafter at bib pickup on race day from 3:00 PM. Late registration fee: 300 SEK (M/K), 200 SEK (Children/Youth). The P/F11 and younger classes have no timing/prize awarding. Trail race along First Camp Löttorp with start times for different age classes: P/F7 (800 m), P/F9 (1.4 km), P/F11 (1.4 km) and P/F13 (1.4 km).

name: Falkenbergs Stadslopp

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 400 kr fram till och med 14:e juli 2026.

description: Falkenbergs Stadslopp is a well-attended 10 km city race that runs through Falkenbergs central streets and green spaces. The race is held on Saturday, 25 July 2026 with a mass start at 12:00 and suits both experienced runners and recreational runners. For 2026 the course has a new route due to municipal works at Doktorspromenaden, and the event offers a festive atmosphere with crowd support along the course. The event has been organized for over 40 years and is part of Tour de Falkenberg.
course_highlights: 10 km through the city's central areas and green spaces
New course layout in 2026 due to works at Doktorspromenaden
Start at Falkenbergs Idrottsplats (new start location) and finish in the city center at Nygatan / Stortorget
additional: Distance: 10 km with separate women's and men's classes; the course is measured by Svenska Friidrottsförbundet; award ceremony around 13:00 and a medal for every runner at the finish. Self-seeded mass start with start corrals marked by time flags (e.g., 4:30/km). Water at the start plus two water stations along the course. Bib pickup at Team Sportia (Lokstallarna, Sandgatan 40) on Thursday and Friday of the same week from 12:00-18:00, and on Saturday at the start area from 09:00. Bag drop-off at the start area from 10:00, to be collected no later than 15:00. No refunds of the registration fee, but the organizers can assist with name changes. The race is part of Tour de Falkenberg and constitutes the district championships 2026. 10 km course through Falkenberg's central areas; start Läroverksgatan and finish Nygatan/Stortorget; 2026 course change due to Doktorspromenaden.

name: Bjäre Trail
description: Bjäre Trail is a trail race on the beautiful Bjäre Peninsula with a very hilly course along the northern side of Hallandsås. You run through Sinarpsdalen, dense beech forests with cascading waterfalls, and past pastures, a closed-down ski slope, and an old railway – the course offers many magical views. The website lists several distances (12 km, 17 km, 34 km and 51 km) and a children's race. Welcome to sign up and experience a demanding but nature-focused trail experience.
course_highlights: Very hilly course along the northern side of Hallandsås Ridge
Passes through Sinarpsdalen and dense beech forests with cascading waterfalls
Includes pastures, a closed-down ski slope, and an old railway with magical views
additional: Start and finish at Båstad Företagsby, Ängelholmsvägen 269, 42 Båstad. Barn/juniorloppet är cirka 2 000 m och anmäls på plats (kontant eller Swish) för 60 kr. Webbplatsen erbjuder PM, startlista, tidigare resultat och GPS-fil (.gpx) för bansträckning. Max 300 startande; anmälan via hemsidan; sista ordinarie anmälningsdag en vecka före start; efteranmälan på tävlingsdagen mot extra avgift. Nummerlappar hämtas vid start/mål senast en timme före start eller i Bjäre bär’s gårdsbutik. Toaletter finns i företagsbyn; omklädningsrum och duschar finns inte. Rekommenderad resa med Skånetrafiken.

name: Hamra Trail Run 2026
description: Hamra Trail Run is a small, family-friendly trail race in a fantastic mountain environment with a focus on the experience rather than a mass start. The race is offered in three distances – Sprint 12 km, Distance 24 km, and Ultra 48 km – and starts from Pensionat Strandgården in Fjällnäs, Tänndalen. With a limited number of starting spots (max 150), the organizers invite participants to enjoy views from Skenörsfjället, camaraderie, and a runner's dinner after the finish.
course_highlights: The courses mostly run on existing trails and paths in the mountain landscape
Ascents up and down Skenörsfjället with views toward Malmagsvålen
Start and bib distribution at Pensionat Strandgården, Fjällnäs
additional: Mandatory equipment: own cup (no disposable cups at hydration checkpoints), insulating layer for the upper body, wind jacket (and possibly wind pants), buff, first aid kit including Dauerlinda and a mobile phone with a saved emergency number. Max 150 participants; registration via MittLopp.se (links from the organizer). GPX files and a PM with the emergency number and practical information will be published before the race. After the race there will be a mingle and prize-giving at 15:00 as well as a runner's dinner. No studs or metal cleats allowed; volunteers with first aid training will be stationed. Max 150 start places; registration via MittLopp.se; GPX files in The Runner's Guide to HTR; pre-race briefing 30 minutes before the start outside Strandgården; hydration stations along the course; accommodation at Strandgården or Fjällnäs; After Run and runner's dinner; start times: 48k 08:00, 24k 10:00, 12k 11:30.

name: Salomon 27K
location: Ottsjö, Åre Municipality, Jämtland County, Sweden
description: Salomon 27K is a 27-kilometer mountain running event that is part of Fjällmaratonveckan and traverses three mountains, with a picturesque finish in Ottsjö. The race is described as scenic and by many as one of Sweden's most beautiful. The course is pure mountain terrain with spectacular views and challenging running over mountain sections.
course_highlights: 27 kilometers of mountain terrain
Runs over three mountains
Finish in Ottsjö with beautiful surroundings
additional: Food and drink stations along the course (see preliminary menu), mug-free drink stations with a kåsa, bus transfers to the start from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker and back after finishing, electronic timing with chip, safety organization on the mountain, option to transfer your entry for a fee (250 kr), recommendation to use the Startklar insurance. Results and live updates are available; start location can be transferred if needed; sponsors include Kia and Fjälltransfer Partners

name: Ottsjö 12k
description: Ottsjö 12K is a 12 km mountain race with about 300 meters of elevation gain that offers a beautiful but demanding course in alpine terrain. The race is an alternative for those who want to experience the mountain landscape without tackling the full distance or the Salomon 27K. The course goes from the start in Ottsjö up toward Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas wind shelters, continues along the plateau trail past Platåkåtan, and finishes downhill through the village along Ottsjön to the finish on the meadows in Ottsjö. The organizers offer a family option (children 10 - 13 run with an adult for 200 kr) and youths 14 - 18 get half the registration fee.
course_highlights: Alpine terrain with about 300 meters of elevation gain
Ascent toward Petterfjället and the Kläpphögarnas wind shelters, and along the plateau trail past Platåkåtan
Finish downhill through the village and along Ottsjön to the finish on the meadows in Ottsjö
additional: Start times are given as 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30. Possibility to run with children 10 - 13 years for 200 kr; age limit otherwise 14 years. Youths 14 - 18 years pay half the registration fee. Electronic timing with chip, food and drink stations with locally produced artisanal foods; a kåsa is used at mug-free stations. Bus transfers to the start from Ottsjö, Trillevallen and Undersåker, as well as bus transfers back after finish. 12 km, ~300 m elevation gain; start in Ottsjö; child version 10 - 13 years for 200 kr with an adult; age limit 14 years; accompanying runners must stay in contact with minors; 14 - 18 years pay half price; start times: 26/7 at 13:00 and 1/8 at 10:30.

name: Peak Performance Vertical K
description: Peak Performance Vertical K is a prestigious, fast and demanding uphill race that is held annually on Tuesday evenings during the Kia Fjällmaraton. The race has a mass start from Åre Torg and finishes at the top of Åreskutan, with exactly 1000 vertical meters. Expect maximum effort from start to finish; the course records to beat are Emmie Collinges 46:24 and Kilian Jornet's 39:13. The organizers collaborate with Peak Performance, who have developed a training program for the race for those who want to prepare specifically for Vertical K.
course_highlights: Mass start from Åre Torg
Finish at the top of Åreskutan - exactly 1000 vertical meters
Fast, steep uphill section; course records: Emmie Collinges 46:24, Kilian Jornet's 39:13
additional: Prize money is awarded to the top 3 in the men's and women's classes. The organizers have created a 6-week training program in the Peak Performance Strava club. A map image is published (map_verticalk.png on the site). Uniquely, it is Sweden's only vertical kilometer according to sources; part of Fjällmaraton week (Kia Fjällmaratonveckan) and AXA Fjällmaratonveckan according to a blog post; the course is said to be about 5 km long according to the blog, and there is a training link via the Peak Performance Strava club.

name: ATEA Kalmarmilen
description: ATEA Kalmarmilen is an established 10-kilometer race in Kalmar that takes place on July 29, 2026, and welcomes both recreational runners and elite runners. The start is at Teatervallen and the finish area is Larmtorget, with a course that passes Kalmar slott, Stensö, Gamla stan, hamnen, Fredrikskans, Lindö and Ängö before the final stretch back to the city center. The race also serves as DM/VDM-status for Östsvenska and is organized by Högby IF, while being part of the I Run Kalmar-race series. On the same day, Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen is held for children in various age classes, making the day a family event with several running options.
course_highlights: Start at Teatervallen and finish at Larmtorget in Kalmar
The course passes Kalmar slott, Stensö, Gamla stan, hamnen, Fredrikskans, Lindö and Ängö
Illuminated running tracks and fitness trails in Kalmar; Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen for children is held simultaneously
additional: Högby IF's athletics page lists several upcoming races (including Kalmar Backyard Ultra, Skälbyloppet, Ölands Tjurrus) with specified dates and start times. The pages mention GPX files and a map of the course as well as a walking class (Skälbyloppet: 4 km without timing) and separate start times for youth and senior classes. Bib pickup at Kalmar Teater on 28 July from 15:00-17:00 and 29 July from 15:00-19:00. ICA MAXI offers drinks, fruit and chocolate after the race. Lilla Atea Kalmarmilen is held simultaneously for children 2-13 years old; the main race has a main distance of 10 km and mini-classes and distances for younger age groups.

name: Fjällmaraton 100k
description: Fjällmaraton 100K is a long and classic mountain run that starts at dawn in Fångåmon and is part of Kia Fjällmaraton Årefjällen. The first part of the course is a beautiful, winding and runnable trail toward Vålådalen via Nulltjärn, before it connects to the classic Fjällmaraton stretch over the dominant Ottfjället. Runners continue over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste on the way back to the finish in Ottsjö. The race character is demanding and self-supported - participants must manage fluids and nutrition themselves between the official aid stations.
course_highlights: Beautiful, winding and runnable route toward Vålådalen via Nulltjärn
Classic ascent over the dominant Ottfjället
Passages over Hållfjället, Grofjället and Välliste with alpine terrain
additional: All participants must be self-supported during the race - refill at official aid stations or use natural springs; support outside the official stations is not allowed. Official sports drink: U Sport by Umara (lemon, blend 90 g/l) and gluten-free U-bars are available at the stations. Important stations and approximate distances: Vålådalen 22 km, Nordbottnen 38 km, Ottsjö (drop bag) 51.5 km, Tobaksdalen 65 km, Edsåsdalen 77.5 km, Skavhugget 82.5 km, Ytterstvallen 92.5 km, Finish 100 km. Post-race food served from Fävikens Lanthandel. The organizers run Ottsjö 8K in the evening to create a good atmosphere at the finish. Drop bag is available at Ottsjö (51.5 km); official energy drink U Sport by Umara and gluten-free U-bars are mentioned in the general information; start time 05:00; approximately 3300 meters of elevation gain; transfer and travel options via Kia Fjälltransfer during Fjällmaraton Week.

name: Bruksleden Terrängmaraton
description: Welcome to Bruksleden Trail Marathon, a family-friendly trail run along the beautiful Bruksleden on Saturday, August 1, 2026. The race offers two distances: 42 km (the Full) and 21 km (the Half), and suits both experienced trail runners and curious recreational runners. The courses pass through forests, on winding trails and past lakes, with varied and sometimes technically demanding terrain. The number of starting spots is limited to preserve the convivial atmosphere and along the course there are staffed checkpoints; after finishing, a shower and a light meal are offered.
course_highlights: Running on Bruksleden's winding forest trails
Sections passing by lakes and beautiful forest scenery
Varied, sometimes technical terrain with steep ascents and descents
additional: Two distances: 42 km (the Full) and 21 km (the Half). Limited number of starting spots: 200. The last day for regular registration is 17 July 2026; late registration until 30 July 2026 with a 50% increased fee. Along the course there are staffed checkpoints for refilling. The course profile and route (21 km and 42 km) and map materials are published on the organizer's pages. The organizers reserve the right to make adjustments to the course. Gathering/start time is 10:00; after finishing, a shower and a light meal are offered. Limited starting numbers for the Full and the Half, up to about 200 participants. The finish area at Fageråsen includes showers and catering.

name: Kia Fjällmaraton 45 km
description: Kia Fjällmaraton 45K is a demanding mountain marathon over classic alpine terrain, during Fjällmaraton Week in the Åre area. The race dates back to 2005, and for 2026 the course is planned to traverse Ottfjället along the organizer’s signature route. The race welcomes both experienced mountain runners and curious beginners seeking an unusual and scenic challenge. To obtain the well-known wooden medal you must finish within the 'medal time' (the winning time + 30%); all participants must be self-sufficient on the course.
course_highlights: The course goes over Ottfjället on classic alpine terrain
Food and drink stations at Edsåsdalen (12 km, 25 km), Tobaksdalen (35.5 km), and Hållvallen (40 km)
Finish in Ottsjö with a communal post-race lunch for all finishers
additional: Participants must be self-sufficient on the course; the official hydration product at the stations is Umara (2:1 lemon, 120 g/l). There are water and toilets at the start in Trillevallen. Support along the course is not allowed beyond the official stations. The stations offer, in addition to drinks, bars, bananas, buns and, at later stations, also hot sausages, coffee and broth. The race is approximately 45 km long with around 1200 meters of elevation gain (according to race report). Participants are self-sufficient between depots; official hydration and food distribution are at Edsåsdalen, Tobaksdalen and Hållvallen. Fjälltransfer is offered by Kia for free transfer between finish and parking as well as a bus between finish and Undersåker/Åre, and lodging in Åre near Kia Fjällmaraton includes, among others, Hotel Åre Fjällsätra.

name: PRB (Växjö)
description: PRB is a Backyard Ultra event in Växjö that, in 2026, will be held as a Silver Ticket event. Participants run a lap of 6,706 meters with starts every full hour; the first start is at 10:00 and the race follows last-man-standing rules in accordance with general Backyard Ultra principles. The course is varied and easy to run, with both asphalt and gravel/trail sections to enable participants to stay in the race as long as possible. The turning and finish are at the southern shore of Trummen, with services in the turning area for runners and accompanying persons.
course_highlights: Lap of 6,706 meters - 24 laps equal 100 miles (160.93 km)
Approximately 35 meters of elevation gain per lap
Approximately 3 km of asphalt per lap, the remainder gravel and trail; turning at the southern shore of Trummen near a playground, skate park and swimming area
additional: The organizer offers an energy table in the turning area with sport drink (Umara), water, Coca-Cola, coffee, candy, chips and fruit; cooked meals are served every six hours with the first service after four hours. A medal is awarded for completing at least one lap and a Finisher Beer from Tomorrow Brewing awaits at the finish. Participants are allowed to pitch small tents and chairs in the turning area. The nearest bus stop is Trummenvägen (line 3) and the recommended parking is at Ica Kvantum Teleborg (fee ~10 SEK per day). Participants who choose to withdraw must notify the race management to obtain a result; you may not cross the start line and turn back (the course is one-way), but you may pass the line to change clothes, eat, use the toilet, etc. Energy and drink stations with sport drink, water, cola, coffee, candy, chips and fruit; meals are served every six hours (start after four hours). A medal is awarded for completing at least one lap and a Finisher Beer waits at the finish. The event indicates easy access to public transport and parking regulations.

name: ÖTILLÖ Gothenburg
description: ÖTILLÖ Swimrun Gothenburg is a well-established swimrun race in the southern Gothenburg archipelago, built on a strong local tradition. The event offers three distances - Experience, Sprint and World Series - and features varied running and many short open-water swims between granite islands. The start and finish area at Styrsö Bratten is easily accessible with frequent ferry connections, and the organizer highlights spectator-friendly views and a summer-friendly race setup. The schedule and practical information (ferries, bib distribution, etc.) are published on the race page prior to the races.
course_highlights: Constant land-to-water transitions with many short, intense swimming sections (island-hopping)
Varied terrain on granite islands - fast trails, rocks, and hilly sections
Spectator-friendly and easily accessible via several daily ferry departures to Styrsö Bratten
additional: Schedule and practical information: bib distribution at the gym at Styrsöskolan (Friday 16:00 - 17:00 for Experience/Sprint/World Series; Saturday morning according to the timetable), fixed ferry times recommended (departures from Stenpiren/Saltholmen to Styrsö Bratten), and the price for World Series includes timing, live tracking if needed, safety concept with safety boats at swimming sections, energy stations along the course and free post-race food and drinks at the finish. Distance-specific facts: World Series ~39,200 m (29 running, 28 swimming), Sprint ~22,400 m (18 running, 17 swimming), Experience ~8,800 m (8 running, 7 swimming). Start and finish at Styrsö Brattenbadet; ferry traffic from Saltholmen or Stenpiren to access the competition area; limited parking at Saltholmen; recommended use of public transport and the Västra Västerås To Go app for ferry tickets and schedules; plan your trip in advance and be in the starting field on time.

name: TGS - Trail Genom Skåne
description: TGS - Trail Genom Skåne is a trail race that offers running on beautiful trails in Göinge and Hovdala Nature Reserve with start and finish at Trädhuset (Hovdala, Hässleholm). The event offers four distances (TGS 60, 35, 25 and 10), where TGS 60 is run as two laps (35+25). A new route for 2026 is more technical and has a reduced asphalt portion (under 3 km) for closer contact with nature. The race suits runners of different levels who want to enjoy forest terrain and well-marked courses.
course_highlights: Running on beautiful trails in Göinge and Hovdala Nature Reserve
TGS 60 is two laps (35+25) – more technical course with under 3 km of asphalt
Hydration stations at km 13.2 and 24.6; start/finish at Trädhuset (Hovdala)
additional: Start and finish at Trädhuset (Hovdala, Hässleholm). TGS 60: 61.7 km with 1060 m D+ / D- (maximum time 9h15m, rep time at the lap turn at 13:30). TGS 35: 35.1 km, 600 m+/-, start 09:30, finish closes 17:00. TGS 25: 26.6 km, 460 m+/-, start 10:45, finish closes 17:00. TGS 10: 10.2 km, 200 m+/-, start 13:45. Hydration stations (HS) offer food, water, cola and sports drink (listed at km 13.2 and 24.6 depending on distance). Registration is binding after payment; the organizer recommends that runners obtain a recreational-running insurance. Start: Trädhuset at Hovdala; various distances (50, 25/27, 10 km); restrictions such as no trekking poles and to carry a mobile phone, water and energy; maximum/target times according to the website; free parking near start/finish; hydration stations as needed during warm days; results and food after the race.

name: Halland Ultra Beach Trailrun
organizer: Benen på Ryggen Adventures; Svalhögens IF
description: Halland Ultra-Beach (HUB) is a coastal ultramarathon in the West Coast landscape that celebrates open trail running. The race consists of six stages between Gothenburg and Båstad and offers distances from individual stages (40–72 km) up to the full race at 100 km, 100 miles and 200 miles. The courses often run along the coastline and vary between sand, trails, pastures and more rugged terrain; runners navigate using digital maps/GPX and are largely self-sufficient between controls. The organizers offer stations with hot food and energy from Umara as well as some bag transport and drop-bag service for the longer distances.
course_highlights: Six stages along the west coast between Gothenburg and Båstad, mostly along the shoreline
Varied surfaces: beaches, trails, pastures and sections without clear paths (some water crossings occur)
Unpaved and unmarked across large parts - navigate with a digital map/GPX (keep the sea on your right)
additional: Early-bird discount is valid until 2025-09-30; registration is open until 2026-07-26 with very limited opportunity for late registration. Maximum entries: 60 starting spots for 200M and 100M; 30 starting spots per individual stage. For 100k, 100M and 200M, something edible is offered as well as drop-bag service at the end of each stage. Start kit with digital map, roadbook and GPX file provided; baggage transfer to the finish and hot food/drink at controls and at the finish. The race is largely self-supported between controls and partially unmarked. Umara energy products at stations; starter kit with maps and digital route description as well as GPX files; Hub Five-Days offers five day stages (75/64/51/51/87 km) with lodging options as well as pacing and guidance services; registration is via Race-ID for Five-Days.

name: Ölands Marathon
description: Ölands Marathon is an open marathon race with start and finish on the square in Löttorp. The course is very flat and fast to run, fully paved, and offers views toward Blå Jungfrun. The race consists of an inner loop of 2.1 km and an outer loop of 11.2 km that are repeated three times until 42.195 km is reached. The race is organized by Högby IF and targets recreational runners and veteran classes according to the specified classes.
course_highlights: Very flat and fast marathon course
100% asphalt, measured for accuracy by federation course measurer Carl-Gustaf Nilsson
Start and finish on the square in Löttorp; 2.1 km inner loop + 11.2 km outer loop repeated 3 times, view toward Blå Jungfrun
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 12:00. Three aid stations per lap (approximately 13.3 km) serving sports drink (Umara), Coca-Cola and water; own energy supplementation can be handed in no later than one hour before the start. All finishers receive a medal/fossil in Öland limestone; ÖM medals for the first two in each class. Winners in the women’s and men’s classes win a dinner for two at Kalk in Löttorp. Accommodation offered in 4-bed cottages at Högby IP. Hydration stations: three per lap. The course consists of a 2.1 km stretch in Löttorp followed by an 11.2 km stretch Löttorp - Alvedsjö - Kalmarsund - Gudesjö - Löttorp, repeated three times for a total of 42.195 km. Start and finish on the square in Löttorp; accommodation information available via links on the organizer's page.

name: Svartåloppet
description: Svartåloppet is a recurring running event that takes place on the second Saturday in August and brings runners of several distances together. The race offers 14 km and 5.5 km on hilly forest roads and trails, as well as a flat 2.5 km loop on roads. Start and finish are at Svartå Folketshus, and timing is handled by Racetimer, providing modern and reliable result flow. The event caters to both recreational runners and competitive participants and highlights the local nature and network of climbs.
course_highlights: 14 km and 5.5 km: hilly forest terrain on forest roads and trails
2.5 km: flatter loop on roads
Start and finish at Svartå Folketshus
additional: The timing for Svartåloppet is handled by Racetimer, and previous years' results are published via Racetimer. The event is held annually on the second Saturday in August. The contact for the event's responsible party is listed as Svartå Utvecklingsgrupp with phone number 076 3073096. Three distances; medal for the children's class and a goodie bag; registration on-site at the indicated times (09:00 - 10:30) according to information in the event materials.

name: Arctic Circle Race
price_range: 2480 SEK inklusive helikoptertransfer; 1490 SEK utan helikoptertransfer
description: Arctic Circle Race is an off-road race in the middle of the mountains where participants are flown out by helicopter to the start at Guijaure and run about 18 km along the Arctic Circle back to civilization. The race is a mix of adventure and competition and offers an optional helicopter transfer or the possibility to hike to the start on your own. The course is technical and varied with narrow trails, rock slabs and a short but steep ascent called "the Wall." Arctic Circle Race 2026 takes place on Saturday, August 8, 2026, and prices are listed separately for participants with and without a helicopter transfer.
course_highlights: Helicopter drop-off to the start at Guijaure and running along the Arctic Circle (approximately 18 km).
Varied, rocky and often narrow mountain terrain with the steep ascent called 'the Wall' at around 8 km and the last ~4 km a steep descent.
Two aid stations (approximately at 6 km and 12 km); start at 690 m above sea level, highest point 805 m above sea level, finish at 480 m above sea level.
additional: Optional helicopter transfer (with or without helicopter). Share a helicopter by registering several participants at the same time - same bib numbers and the same start time. Check-in, parking and helicopter pickup at Camp Polcirkeln, Polcirkeln 3, 93894 Arjeplog. Timing is done with a chip integrated in the bib. First aid and personnel are available at the aid stations, and a helicopter is on standby for serious incidents. Includes helicopter to the start and the possibility of a round trip Arjeplog - Camp Polcirkeln (round trip) 500 SEK according to information on the English-language page.

name: Bunketorp Backyard Ultra Trail
description: Bunketorp Backyard Ultra Trail is a 'last-man-standing' race in Backyard Ultra format where participants run a 6,706-meter lap every full hour until only one runner remains. The course in Bunketorp, Lindome (south of Gothenburg) runs entirely in forest terrain on well-trodden trails with no asphalt or gravel and offers varied and hilly terrain. The race is organized by IK Uven and offers a personal, family-friendly setup with good service for both runners and supporters. The start for the 2026 edition is Saturday, August 8, 2026 at 10:00.
course_highlights: Lap length 6,706 meters (Backyard Ultra rules)
Soft forest trails with no asphalt or gravel, no long straight sections
Approximately 140 m of elevation gain per lap with three clearly larger climbs
additional: Organizers offer changing rooms with showers and a sauna, at least seven toilets (including portable), 3–5 participant tents and space for own tents. The secretariat handles bib numbers, valuables storage and results; there is a staffed energy depot throughout the event as well as simple refreshments sales for spectators. First aid supplies and a defibrillator are available on-site (no trained medical personnel). There is no age limit; participation is at your own risk. Competition rules: the laps are unidirectional, participants must be in the start corral at every full start and inform the secretariat if they withdraw from the race. Prizes are awarded to the top three women, the top three men, and the best team (three runners). Participants start every hour and must complete one lap within the hour; total 6,706 m per lap; 120 starting places; Silver Ticket for 2026; results are reported to DUV; energy station, fluids, hot meals at certain times, changing facilities, toilets, showers and sauna.

name: Nätra Fjällskogslopp
location: Hinnsjöstugan, Nätra fjällskog, Örnsköldsviks kommun, Sweden
description: Nätra Fjällskogslopp is organized by Nätra GIF ungdom and is a scenic trail run held at Hinnsjöstugan in Nätra fjällskog. The first race took place in 2021, and the competition offers challenging yet enjoyable courses through forests, boardwalks over marshland, and winding trails with beautiful views. There are four distances (22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km for children) and the organizers encourage both competitive runners and recreational participants to choose their place in the start field according to their own capacity. Start and finish at Hinnsjöstugan with clear markings and services for participants.
course_highlights: Trails, forest roads and boardwalks over marshes – varied trail running
Views from Västerselsbodarna and Västanåhöjden (the possibility to glimpse Ulvön)
Long downhill sections toward the finish with a view over Hinnsjön
additional: Organizer: Nätra GIF ungdom. Start location: Startstugan Hinnsjön (address Hinnsjön 100, Sidensjö). Parking is indicated along the road near Hinnsjöstugan, a short walk to the start. Bib numbers must be picked up no later than 09:00 for the 22 km, 15 km and 9 km. Clothing drop-off is available at Hinnsjöstugan. Recommended equipment: mobile phone, fluids/energy and a map of the course. Start times: 22 km 09:30, 15 km 09:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. Distance markers have different colors (22/15 blue/yellow, 9 red/yellow, 2 yellow). Participants are encouraged to stay on marked trails, use the boardwalks and bring trash to the finish. After the course, two nature reserves are passed (Västanåhöjdens and Stakamyras) with special regulations. The distances are 22 km, 15 km, 9 km and 2 km (children). Start times according to information: 22 km 9:30, 15 km 9:45, 9 km 10:00, 2 km 10:10. The event runs as a full-day activity 10:30 - 16:00 and is listed as fully booked.

name: Ångaloppet Trail
description: Ångaloppet is a welcoming swimrun event at Ånga gård with the goal 'swimrun for everyone'. The 2026 races take place on August 8 and include several distances and events for different levels, including 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. The courses offer varied nature with forest trails, gravel roads and hilly technical terrain; the swimrun runs also include several swimming sections in both freshwater and the sea. The organizers emphasize an inviting atmosphere for participants of all ages and experience levels.
course_highlights: Varied forest, trails and gravel roads
Hilly and technical terrain suitable for trail running
Located between Lake Ången and the Baltic Sea - a combination of running and swimming (for the swimrun distances)
additional: In 2026 the event consists of five races on the same day (8 August): 22 km, 11 km, Trail, 5 km and Family. For the 22 km race: loop course (11 km per lap), total ~20 swim sections (longest about 190 m, shortest about 30 m), six aid stations along the course and a 2.5-hour cut-off time at the lap turn. Team changes are possible for a fee of 400 SEK - email info@angaloppet.se. The courses are marked and start group 1 (earliest start) is at 10:00. Ångaloppet Trail is a new distance in the 2026 program. Team changes possible for a fee of 400 SEK. More information about equipment, safety, accommodation and parking can be found on the event pages.

name: Stora Stöten Run
description: Stora Stöten Run is a trail race in the World Heritage Site of the Falun Mine, offering a historic and varied running experience. The course passes medieval smelting sites, miners' cottages, ponds and dam houses, and follows old trail networks called The Water's Path to the Mine. The race has three distances (21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km) and targets both competitive runners and recreational runners with the option to choose timing or to run without timing. The organizer is the orienteering club OK Kåre, which welcomes participants to the start and finish at Falun Mine.
course_highlights: Three courses: 21.6 km, 13.6 km and 5.6 km with start/finish at Falun Mine
The course passes medieval smelting sites, miners' cottages, ponds and dam houses along The Water's Path to the Mine
Varied surfaces: gravel, grass, cross-country trails, nature trails and short sections of asphalt; initial climb and clear downhill sections
additional: Start and finish at Falun Mine; warm-up starts at 12:10 at Falu Rödfärg's asphalt area (about 7 minutes) led by Friskis & Svettis; all courses start at the same time and runners are divided into two optional groups based on finish pace (Group 1: women ≤ 6 min/km, men ≤ 5 min/km). It is optional to run with or without timing; prizes for the first three on each course and raffle prizes for the other participants; opportunity to register a team (team of 3) and to transfer your registration free of charge via the registration system; energy stations and water stations, parking, race office, showers/changing rooms, and course markings are mentioned in the competition information. Three courses with start and finish at Falun Mine; previous years' results are available.

name: Kräftivalloppet
description: Kräftivalloppet is a running competition in Tidaholm that is part of Kraftivalen and takes place near Gamla torget. The adult race requires registration via motionsloppet.se, while the children's and senior races are without pre-registration. Warm-up before the races is conducted in collaboration with Hälsocenter, and the event is open to the whole family. The children's race for ages 7 and up is about 600 meters per lap (maximum three laps), the walker/rollator and senior race around 600 meters, and children from age 2 about 400 meters.
course_highlights: Part of Kraftivalen in Tidaholm with start area around Gamla torget
The adult race requires pre-registration via motionsloppet.se; the children's and senior races are without pre-registration
Short children's and senior races with distances around 400-600 meters per lap
additional: Warm-up before the races in collaboration with Hälsocenter

name: Istrun - Skaras snabba halvmara
description: Istrun - Skara's Fast Half Marathon is a half marathon organized by I strums SK - Athletics in Skara. The race name emphasizes that the course is fast and targets runners who want to run a fast half marathon. Currently the race is sold out, but the organizer offers a waiting list for interested runners. For questions or to join the waiting list, please email istrun@istrumssk.se.
course_highlights: Half marathon in Skara (marketed as "Skara's Fast Half Marathon")
additional: The race is currently sold out; interested runners can join a waiting list by emailing istrun@istrumssk.se. All information about the competition refers to Istrums SK - Athletics. Registrations are handled via RaceID and for runners who do not belong to the club, registration is recommended in M Motion or K Motion according to the page text. PB note: a participant mentions a PB of 1:47:29 in a Facebook post.

name: Häv och Gräv Vikbovändan 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: vuxen 470 kr (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar loppet 520 kr)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: duoklass: 940 kr per par (fram till den 30/6, sedan kostar duolopp 1040 kr)

description: Häv & Gräv Vikbovändan is a summer race on Vikbolandet in Östergötland where you can choose to run or cycle. The main course is about 45 km long and runs largely on country roads and gravel (roughly 50/50), with several energy stations and tastings from local farms along the route.
